guidance: Use it for one game line or a whole season; ice time takes mm:ss or decimal minutes. Enter only goals charged to the goaltender and only shots the official scorer counted, because empty-net goals, shootout goals and shootout saves are not part of GAA or save percentage. Shots faced is derived as saves plus goals against, so the numbers cannot contradict each other, and a goaltender who faced no shots shows a dash instead of an invented percentage.
method: Minutes played are accepted as mm:ss, where the seconds field must be below 60, or as a decimal number of minutes such as 58.2; a leading colon-free whole number counts as complete minutes. Both forms are converted to whole seconds (mm x 60 + ss, or the decimal rounded to the nearest second) and every rate is computed from that integer, so no fractional minute is rounded twice. The ice time must be at least one second and at most 100,000 minutes, which is 6,000,000 seconds. Goals against and saves must each be whole numbers from 0 to 10,000. Shots against is saves plus goals against, because a shot on goal that scores is counted as a shot and is not a save; that identity is what lets the page derive shots faced without asking for a fourth number that could disagree. Goals against average is 60 x goals against / minutes played, which is also 3,600 x goals against / seconds, and is reported to two decimals like the published statistic. Save percentage is saves / shots against, reported to three decimals in the North American decimal form where .933 means 93.3 percent, together with the same value as a true percentage to one decimal. When shots against is zero the save percentage is undefined and is shown as a dash rather than as a number. Shots against per 60 minutes scales the shot count by 3,600 / seconds. Each figure is rounded half away from zero at the precision it is displayed with. The tool computes from the counts you supply: it does not adjust for team defence, score effects, shot quality, blocked shots or the scorer's judgement, and it does not decide whether a goal should have been charged to the goaltender. Empty-net and shootout goals are excluded from official goals against average, and shootout saves are excluded from official save percentage, so leave them out of the entries. Everything is calculated in this page; nothing is uploaded, stored or fetched.

sources.title: Hockey-Reference NHL Stats Glossary: GAA is goals against divided by minutes played, then multiplied by 60; SV% is saves divided by shots against, and saves are shots against minus goals against.

Wikipedia, Goals against average: for ice hockey a goaltender's goals allowed per 60 minutes, with overtime goals and overtime ice time included but empty-net and shootout goals excluded, usually given to two decimal places.
Wikipedia, Save percentage: saves divided by shots on goal, commonly written as a decimal in North America, so .933 means 93.3 percent of shots were stopped.
